arguments.summary: Policy transmission is differentiated: NVDA has a disclosed China data-center restriction channel and Taiwan/South Korea supply dependency, while MU’s supplied disclosure establishes broad trade/tariff and input-risk channels but does not quantify China, customer, or manufacturing exposure. The dated BIS rule creates a conditional licensing pathway for specified lower-threshold advanced-computing products, not evidence of an approved NVDA transaction or of current complete law. QQQ has dated look-through exposure to both issuers, but those weights do not quantify fund-level policy loss.

claims.text: Effective January 15, 2026, BIS changed license review to case-by-case for specified advanced-computing commodities, including H200 examples, destined to China or Macau if detailed technical, supply, foundry-capacity, shipment-cap, end-user/KYC and testing conditions are met; this is not an automatic export authorization.

NVIDIA's Q3 FY2027 outlook explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China. Its August filing also describes the company as effectively foreclosed from the China market by U.S. export controls, notes Chinese discouragement of its data-center products, and identifies reliance on overseas partners especially in Taiwan and South Korea.

For the 63-session horizon, a qualifying license approval and customer acceptance could be upside optionality for NVDA rather than recovery of revenue embedded in the supplied Q3 outlook, because that outlook excludes China Data Center compute. Conversely, tighter U.S. controls, Chinese implementation of standards that prevent compliant product design, or disruption to Taiwan/South Korea component supply would challenge the assumed demand/margin continuity in any valuation sensitivity. The discriminator is an actual rule amendment or issued license together with NVIDIA disclosure that China revenue is included in outlook, versus a new restriction, rejected/delayed license, Chinese standard implementation, or supply interruption.

Micron discloses that evolving export controls, tariffs and trade barriers may restrict sales to China or other markets, constrain equipment/components/raw materials, raise costs, reduce margins or demand, and cause manufacturing delays. Its June 2026 filing says the scope and outcome of cited Section 232 and Section 301 investigations were unknown at that time.

MU's differentiated policy downside is a broad trade-and-supply-cost shock—new tariffs, export limits on AI-related products or inputs, or retaliatory measures—that impairs availability, cost or customer demand and therefore challenges the high-demand/margin assumptions used elsewhere. A relaxation or a disclosed mitigation that preserves input availability and customer shipments would weaken that downside. The discriminator is a final tariff/export measure or Micron issuer disclosure mapping affected products, facilities, customers, costs, or guidance; no supplied evidence quantifies any of those exposures.
QQQ's September 18, 2026 sponsor holdings view lists NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336%; these are dated fund weights, not current holdings or policy-loss coefficients.

QQQ therefore has a direct look-through channel to both issuer-specific geopolitical shocks, but its broader holdings set means the supplied evidence cannot establish whether fund-level impact is greater or lower than either company’s exposure. A changed QQQ holdings file or a policy event affecting other material constituents would change this comparison.

gaps.description: The supplied January BIS text is dated and no post-rule amendment, license decision, eligibility analysis for a specific NVIDIA product/customer, or verified current legal status is available. This prevents assertions that any sale is currently permitted or quantification of a benefit, but permits the conditional pathway analysis.

No supplied Micron disclosure quantifies revenue by China/end-demand geography, affected product/customer exposure, manufacturing geography, input dependency, or financial sensitivity to a trade action. Do not convert the risk disclosure into a measured loss estimate.
QQQ's dated equity weights establish issuer channels only; excluded cash/derivative positions and the effects of other constituents are not a fund-level geopolitical impact model.

assumptions: This is fixed-evidence analysis as of the task timestamp, not verification of current law or live licensing.
A policy relaxation is treated as optional upside only when it produces a qualifying approval and customer/product eligibility; it is not assumed in NVIDIA's supplied China-excluding outlook.
No revenue, cost, margin, or ETF-loss percentage is inferred from disclosure language or dated weights.
arguments.counter_thesis: The near-term effect could be immaterial if NVDA’s non-China demand and supply continuity offset foregone China optionality, and if Micron’s strategic customer demand and supply arrangements absorb trade friction. The supplied evidence does not measure those offsets, so this is a competing scenario rather than a conclusion.

review_conditions.description: Review NVIDIA's policy scenario if BIS changes the January 2026 eligibility/conditions, a relevant license is approved, denied or delayed, China implements a standard affecting compliant products, or NVIDIA changes guidance to include China Data Center compute; each outcome respectively tests optional upside, restriction downside, or whether China is embedded in assumptions.

Review MU's policy downside upon a final Section 232/301 or export-control action, or Micron disclosure of affected products, inputs, facilities, customer geography, costs or guidance; this would turn the presently unquantified channel into an assessable operating sensitivity.

Review QQQ transmission when sponsor holdings are refreshed following a material policy event, because dated NVDA and MU weights establish a channel but not a persistent composition or fund-level loss.

shared_exposures.mechanism: U.S.-China trade/export measures can transmit through semiconductor product access, customer demand and supply-chain inputs; QQQ's dated holdings include both issuers.
shared_exposures.qualification: The BIS rule is specific to qualifying advanced-computing commodities and dates from January 2026; MU's disclosure describes risks rather than a quantified exposure, and QQQ weights are dated rather than a policy-loss estimate.
